noveltyJustification: All ten findings are new: the hooks.toml declaration shape, the seven events and strict blocking set, hook provenance and protocols, runtime hook context, approval modes, the outside_workdir policy, protected-path escalation, the absence of a CLI sandbox mode, the eight-guard mapping and the turn-stopping gap had no prior capture.
keyQuestions: How does Vibe run one task non-interactively: which prompt source, flags, output formats and exit codes does the headless contract expose?
Which providers, models and authentication paths can a Vibe dispatch use, and which usage counter does a turn draw on?
What does Vibe read from the working directory and ~/.vibe/, and what would a generated repo-root .vibe/ mirror contain?
For each cli-opencode surface this repository uses, does Vibe have an equivalent, a partial equivalent or none, and what would porting take?
What would a cli-mistral-vibe deep-loop executor kind need, and is ACP a better dispatch surface than print mode?
ruledOut: Treating --auto-approve as a sandbox: it only suppresses prompts
Porting completion-evidence as a blocking hook: post_agent has no strict mode
